ava.s: Quick sync — Reef POC is hitting two issues on the embeddings->rerank flow: (1) dims mismatch errors from the reranker, (2) sporadic 429s when they batch more than ~8 items. Can someone pick this up?

lucas.se: On it. Do we have the exact error messages + the model name they're using for encoding vs rerank? My hunch is encoder/model mismatch.

ava.s: Copied from customer: `Error: Invalid vector dimension: expected 1536 but got 768` and `HTTP 429: rate_limited`. They said encoder client is v0.9.1 and calling `POST /v1/embeddings` -> rerank endpoint separately. Model they passed is `open-embed-compat` (customer-provided name).

priya.support: Can you paste the request payload and headers? Also any attachable logs from our side (trace IDs) would help.

ava.s: Pasting their sample request (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
{
  "model": "open-embed-compat",
  "input": ["doc A", "doc B", "doc C"],
  "batch_size": 16
}
```
They included this for reranker: `POST /v1/rerank` with vectors array.

mateo.runtime: Two quick things to check:
1) Vector dim mismatch almost always = encoder and reranker expecting different model dims. Confirm the model metadata (embedding_dim) that our serving runtime reports for `open-embed-compat`. Run `GET /v1/models/open-embed-compat` and compare.
2) 429s at batch_size 16 could be hitting per-route concurrency or token/batch size limits in the runtime. Try batch_size 8 as a quick mitigation.

lucas.se: Also ask the customer whether their client is doing pooling/averaging incorrectly (some libs return 768 for pooled transformer CLS while the model should produce 1536).

priya.support: I pulled the trace for trace_id=trc_0a1b2c3 — server returned `Invalid vector dimension` at our rerank validation layer. Runtime log snippet: 
```
2025-03-11T16:02:12Z ERROR rerank-validator: expected_dim=1536 got=768 request_id=req_7f9
2025-03-11T16:02:12Z INFO caller=ingest: client_id=reef-poc batch_size=16
```

mateo.runtime: That confirms our reranker configured for 1536 on that model variant. Likely the customer's encoder is producing 768 (small model). Action items: ask them to either switch encoder model to one that yields 1536 or use the correct reranker variant for 768.

ava.s: Customer says they thought `open-embed-compat` was an alias mapping to our hosted 1536 model but might be using an on-prem encoder they've built using sentence-transformers `all-MiniLM` (768).

lucas.se: Ok, steps for customer: 1) run `GET /v1/models/open-embed-compat` (we can give them the curl) 2) if they control the encoder, ensure it uses `open-embed-1536` or change reranker to `rerank-compat-768`. Example curl:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models/open-embed-compat | jq
# look for "embedding_dim"
```

priya.support: For the 429s: I checked the last 24h metrics on the route and they peak a lot when batch_size>8. There's a concurrency throttle (per-tenant) set to avoid queueing. We can temporarily increase burst for their sales POC account by raising concurrency by +2 while we triage. Will open internal infra ticket.

mateo.runtime: I'll pre-approve an infra burst for the account for the next 48h. But we should not recommend long-term high batch_size if it violates latency SLOs. Recommend they do client-side chunking into <=8 and async retry on 429 with exponential backoff and jitter.

ava.s: I'll ask the customer to try batch_size=8 and also confirm encoder model. I'll DM them the curl to check model metadata.

lucas.se: Also worth checking whether their encoder output is float16 vs float32; some clients accidentally quantize on client side and our validation can misinterpret that. If they used numpy cast to float16, the shape is same so probably fine, but still call it out.

priya.support: Filed ticket SPT-9182 to track infra burst and logs; attaching trace_id and grouping by client_id=reef-poc.

deploy-bot: deployment #infra-burst-reef accepted by mateo.runtime — increases per-tenant concurrency by 2 for account reef-poc until 2025-03-13T16:02:00Z :rocket:

ava.s: Customer tried batch_size=8 and reran. They still get dim mismatch when they use their on-prem encoder. They agreed to test with our hosted `open-embed-1536` and reported success (rerank accepts vectors). So root cause = encoder model mismatch.

lucas.se: Great, mark this as customer-encoder-mismatch. Recommend we add a short checklist in sales POC doc: verify embedding_dim early, include curl to model metadata, and suggest safe default batch_size=8 for initial POCs.

ava.s: I'll update the POC playbook and send a recap to Reef. Thanks team :thumbsup: 

priya.support: Closing immediate support work but leaving ticket SPT-9182 open until infra burst expires.

mateo.runtime: Follow-up item: product should consider returning a more explicit error message suggesting the detected embedding_dim vs expected and a link to docs. I'll file a small UX task.

lucas.se: Filing doc PR now with the checklist.

ava.s: Awesome — I'll update the deal thread after PR merge. :eyes:
